item.title: FMC Syslog and Audit Log Add-on for Cisco Secure Firewall - v1.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
First release. \- Field extractions for the FMC audit log: logins, policy saves and commits, policy deployments, intrusion rule changes, rule updates and API calls. \- CIM mappings: Authentication and Change (audit log), Alerts (correlation events). \- Event types and tags, exported to all apps. \- Search-time only: install on search heads, including Splunk Cloud and Enterprise Security.


Short Description:
Search-time fields and CIM mappings for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) syslog. Audit log (cisco:fmc:audit): logins, configuration changes, deployments and rule updates for Authentication and Change. Correlation events (cisco:fmc:syslog): Alerts. Works with Enterprise Security. Not affiliated with Cisco.


Description:
Adds search-time field extractions, CIM mappings, event types and tags for the syslog that Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) sends: the audit log and correlation events. - Authentication (cisco:fmc:audit): login success and failure, with the user and, when the FMC logged one, the client address. - Change (cisco:fmc:audit): policy saves and commits, policy deployments, intrusion rule changes, rule update and SRU installs, and API writes, with who made the change and what changed. - Alerts (cisco:fmc:syslog): correlation events, with the rule, policy, source and destination, ports, countries, protocol and severity. - Other audit records (page views, reports, API reads, logouts) get fields and a category but no CIM tags, so they stay out of the data models. - Search-time only: no inputs, index-time settings or dashboards. Install on search heads, including Splunk Cloud and Enterprise Security. - The add-on does not collect data. Send the FMC's syslog to Splunk with these sourcetypes; Installation has the steps. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Cisco.

item.title: Palo Alto Cortex Audit Logs Add-on - v1.0.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Initial release. \- Two inputs for the Palo Alto Networks Cortex public API: \- Audit management logs (sourcetype cortex:audit:management_logs) \- Agent audit reports (sourcetype cortex:audit:agent_reports), with optional category filter (audit / monitoring / status) \- Standard and Advanced API key support; credentials are validated on save and stored in Splunk's encrypted credential store \- HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy support \- Gap-free collection with KV Store checkpointing, configurable start time and ingestion delay \- Automatic retries with backoff for rate limits and server errors \- CIM Authentication data model mapping for console login events \- Requires Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform 10.2 or later (Python 3.13)


Short Description:
Collects audit management logs and agent reports from the Palo Alto Networks Cortex public API and maps authentication events to the CIM Authentication data model.


Description:
The Palo Alto Cortex Audit Logs Add-on collects audit management logs and agent audit reports from the Palo Alto Networks Cortex public API. The add-on retrieves audit data through two dedicated API endpoints: management logs and agent reports. It provides field extractions for both data sources and maps Cortex authentication events to the CIM Authentication data model. The add-on handles data collection in time-windowed increments, maintaining checkpoints to ensure no audit data is skipped during collection cycles. Events are indexed with sourcetypes cortex:audit:management_logs and cortex:audit:agent_reports, making it straightforward to search and analyze Cortex audit activity within Splunk. The add-on assigns event timestamps from the AUDIT_INSERT_TIME field for management logs and the TIMESTAMP field for agent reports. Management log events with AUDIT_ENTITY=AUTH are automatically tagged for the CIM Authentication data model, enabling correlation with other authentication data sources.

item.title: Eventgen Manager - v2.0.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Eventgen Manager 2.0.0 generates events itself. SA-Eventgen is no longer required. NEW Built-in generation engine (eventgen_manager_engine modular input). Pure Python, runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows, on x86 and ARM. Configuration changes apply within seconds. No restart needed. Send test events from the editor to the real destination without turning the configuration on. Live status per configuration: state, events generated, last batch, and the reason for any failure. Automatic timestamps, with a new "Timestamp to write" option: generated time, or current time for testing detections that search the last few minutes. New random values: weighted, ipv4private, email, useragent, uuid. New seqfile replacement. Rated replacements now work. Counters continue from their last value after a restart. verifySSL setting for HEC and Splunk REST receivers. Rebuilt Throughput dashboard: events per second, projected daily volume, failed batches, and configured against measured rates. New Tutorial page with a complete, step-by-step guide. The engine can also run from the command line, outside Splunk. UPGRADING FROM SA-EVENTGEN Existing eventgen.conf configurations work unchanged. If SA-Eventgen is running, the built-in engine waits on standby so events are not doubled. Use "Switch to the built-in engine" on the Generator control page. CHANGED Syslog output now uses TCP. UDP output is removed, as UDP is not allowed on Splunk Cloud or under app certification. To send to indexers over splunktcp, keep the output on modinput and set up forwarding in outputs.conf on the instance running the app. Settings that only tuned SA-Eventgen's worker pools, plugins, and templates are removed from the editor. Existing values are kept in eventgen.conf. FIXED The structured application log starter wrote local time with a "Z" (UTC) suffix. It now sets timezone \= 0000. Tutorial: [https://github.com/genai-telemetry/eventgen-manager/blob/main/Eventgen_Manager_Tutorial.pdf](https://github.com/genai-telemetry/eventgen-manager/blob/main/Eventgen_Manager_Tutorial.pdf)


Short Description:
Configure, preview, and generate realistic test data in Splunk from the browser. A built-in engine runs eventgen.conf configurations directly, with a guided editor, live preview, and throughput monitoring.


Description:
Eventgen Manager configures, previews, and generates realistic test data in Splunk from the browser. A guided editor covers the eventgen.conf settings, so you never hand-edit the file. Pick a sample file, set how often and how many events to send, choose what to replace in each line, and watch a live preview with every generated value highlighted before anything reaches an index. Send test events to the real destination with one click to confirm the index, sourcetype, and output are right. The built-in engine is pure Python and runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows, on x86 and ARM. Changes apply within seconds with no restart. Output goes to the local index, HTTP Event Collector, Splunk REST, files, spool folders, raw TCP, or syslog over TCP. On a heavy forwarder, events are forwarded to your indexers through outputs.conf. Use it for SIEM data , dashboard development, detection and alert testing, training, and load testing. A Throughput dashboard shows events per second, projected daily volume, failed batches, and configured against measured rates.

item.title: EventLab - v1.0.3 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
Security \- Removed the automatic HTTP fallback added in 1.0.2. When a secure connection to the Splunk management port failed, 1.0.2 retried over plain HTTP, which sent the Splunk session key unencrypted. In typical installs this traffic stayed on the local machine. EventLab now picks HTTP or HTTPS only from Splunk's own configuration. All 1.0.2 users should upgrade. Splunk Cloud compatibility \- Python version settings now meet Splunk Cloud requirements (Python 3.9 and 3.13), so the app can be installed on Splunk Cloud again. Fixes and improvements \- Correctly detects when the Splunk management port runs without SSL. \- HEC Auto-Configure warns you if the global HTTP Event Collector setting could not be enabled, instead of reporting success. \- Clearer guidance when a connection fails because of SSL settings. \- Management addresses with a trailing slash or an IPv6 host now work. \- Added documentation for all eventlab.conf settings. Compatibility \- Requires Splunk with Python 3.9 or newer (Splunk Enterprise 9.3+ or 10.x, or Splunk Cloud). Not supported on Splunk 9.2 or earlier. Upgrading \- Upgrading from 1.0.2 keeps your HEC token, AI provider settings and saved data.


Short Description:
AI-powered synthetic data generator for Splunk. Creates realistic security events, simulates 54 MITRE ATT&CK techniques, builds custom models from real logs, and validates output quality with statistical tests — all through natural-language commands. Supports multiple LLM providers, including a fully air-gapped option.


Description:
EventLab is an AI-powered synthetic data generator built as a native Splunk application. It enables SOC analysts, detection engineers, and Splunk administrators to produce realistic synthetic security events on demand — for testing detections, populating training environments, validating SPL queries, and running live demonstrations — without exposing real production data. The built-in AI assistant accepts plain-English commands: generate a fixed batch, start a continuous real-time stream, simulate a MITRE ATT&CK technique, or schedule recurring jobs. Every generated batch is statistically validated against real production data, giving teams a measurable quality score that proves synthetic events match production patterns. EventLab ships with prebuilt models for common log sources — Palo Alto firewall, Windows Security, DNS, web access, and Linux syslog — and can build new models directly from your Splunk indexes. The AI profiles real events, extracts field types and token patterns, and produces a generation-ready model in minutes. Key capabilities: - 22 AI-driven tools for generation, streaming, scenario simulation, quality assessment, and model authoring. - 54 preconfigured MITRE ATT&CK techniques spanning all 14 tactics. - Statistical quality scoring: Kolmogorov–Smirnov, chi-squared, and temporal cosine similarity tests. - Real-time streaming with configurable EPS and rate patterns (flat, spike, ramp, burst). - Scheduled generation via cron expressions for continuous data feeds. - Multi-LLM provider support: Anthropic Claude, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and Ollama for fully air-gapped deployments. - Multi-tenancy with four RBAC roles, owner-scoped data isolation, and six granular capabilities. - Full audit trail logged to KV Store and Splunk indexes. Who it is for: - SOC teams running detection engineering, content development, and analyst training. - Splunk administrators needing realistic data for performance testing and demos. - Security architects validating SIEM pipelines without exposing customer data. - Educators and trainers building hands-on Splunk labs.

item.title: ShadowTrackr - v1.2.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Bring your external attack surface into Splunk. ShadowTrackr finds your internet-facing hosts, websites, certificates, CVEs, lookalike domains and suppliers; this app puts them in dashboards, detections and Enterprise Security, and adds attack surface context to your firewall, proxy and auth logs with one command.


Description:
**See your organization the way attackers do, right inside Splunk.** Most breaches start at the edge: a forgotten test server, an expired certificate, an exposed RDP port, a website running vulnerable software, or a lookalike domain set up for phishing. ShadowTrackr (External Attack Surface Management) continuously discovers and monitors everything you have on the internet. This app brings all of it into Splunk, so your SOC can alert on it, correlate it with your own logs and act on it in the tools it already uses. **What you get** - **Events and alerts.** Every ShadowTrackr finding (new open ports, vulnerabilities, certificate problems, blacklistings, leaked data, phishy domains) arrives as CIM-mapped events. Optionally, ShadowTrackr alerts push straight into Splunk by webhook within seconds. - **A full asset inventory in the KV Store.** Hosts, websites, domains, certificates, DNS, software and CVEs, cloud providers, exposed email addresses, phishy domains and suppliers, refreshed automatically. - **Six dashboards.** A posture overview, vulnerabilities and software (CVSS, CISA KEV, NCSC NL, known exploited), certificates, supplier dependency, a live search explorer, and Asset 360, which pivots from one asset to your own firewall, proxy, WAF, authentication and IDS logs. - **Ready-made detections.** 12 detections and 3 health checks, all shipped disabled so you choose. Examples: an attack on an asset with known CVEs, a successful login from the internet on an exposed remote access service, users visiting lookalikes of your domains, a risky port that opens, a certificate about to expire. - **Enterprise Security.** Correlation searches with notable events, risk-based alerting and MITRE ATT&CK annotations, plus an ES asset lookup of your internet-facing assets. - **Enrich any search.** `| stenrich field=dest_ip` tells you whether an IP or hostname is one of your internet-facing assets, and what is open, vulnerable or misconfigured on it. It uses only the local lookups and makes no API calls. - **Supplier dependency.** See which suppliers hold your assets, where they are headquartered and controlled from (Sovereign European, Fully European, European subsidiary, Non-European), and how many are outside the EU. Useful for NIS2 and digital sovereignty. **Built for production.** API keys are stored encrypted in the Splunk credential store. Read-only keys and MSSP group keys are supported, as are proxies, checkpointing and automatic backfill. The app passes Splunk AppInspect, including the Splunk Cloud checks. Requires a ShadowTrackr Business or Enterprise subscription for API access. Start a free trial at https://shadowtrackr.com.

item.title: Advisory IOC Sweeper - v1.4.0 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Short Description:
Upload a threat advisory (PDF, scanned PDF, DOCX, XLSX, EML, HTML or screenshot), review the IOCs it contains, and sweep 15 CIM data models for them with tstats in minutes. Includes drill-down, sweep history, an executive PDF report, an Alert Builder for scheduled alerts and ES detections, and STIX, EDL and hash exports. Runs fully on-prem.


Description:
Advisory IOC Sweeper turns any threat advisory into a hunt across your Splunk data in a few minutes. When a new advisory arrives from CISA, a national CERT, a vendor or your threat intel provider, someone has to copy the IPs, domains, URLs and hashes out of a PDF, undo the defanging (hxxp, [.], [@]), write the searches and work out whether any of it ever touched your environment. This app does that whole job inside Splunk Enterprise. Upload the advisory as a text or scanned PDF, DOCX, XLSX, EML, HTML, TXT/CSV/JSON or a PNG/JPG screenshot. The app extracts IPv4, IPv6, networks, domains, URLs, email addresses, MD5, SHA1, SHA256, SHA512, file names and CVE IDs, refangs every common defang style and shows each indicator with the line it came from. Likely IOCs are pre-ticked by a clear, documented rule set, and noise such as the publisher's own domain, reference links and private IPs is flagged or excluded. You stay in control: tick, untick, add missed indicators or allowlist them. One click sweeps the committed IOCs with tstats across 18 datasets in 15 CIM data models (Network Traffic, DNS, Web, Authentication, IDS, Endpoint, Malware, Email, Vulnerabilities, Certificates and more), including IOCs hidden inside command lines and registry values. Results show what was seen, where and by which hosts and users, with drill-down to the raw events. Then act on it: an executive Sweep Report ready for PDF export, an optional Sweep History in a summary index, an Alert Builder for scheduled alerts and Enterprise Security detections, and exports to CSV, JSON, STIX 2.1, firewall EDL lists and EDR hash lists. Everything runs locally on your search heads. No cloud service, no API keys and no outbound connections.

Description:
TrackMe Broker lets TrackMe on Splunk Cloud reach the systems on your own network: remote Splunk instances (Heavy Forwarders, Deployment Servers), self-managed Cribl Leaders and webhook receivers. From a Splunk Cloud stack those destinations cannot be reached, because the stack cannot connect into your network. TrackMe Broker reverses the direction. This add-on runs on a Heavy Forwarder on your side, asks the stack for work over its REST API on port 8089, makes the HTTPS call locally and posts the answer back. Every connection starts on your side: you open nothing inbound. - Deny by default: the forwarder reaches only the targets you declare on it, whatever the stack asks for. - Encrypted end to end: each request and response is sealed for one paired forwarder (AES-256-GCM, keys on P-256), on top of HTTPS. - Paired, not trusted blindly: you accept each forwarder in TrackMe after checking its key fingerprint. - Highly available: run two forwarders in one broker; they share the work, and one carries on if the other stops. - Least privilege, FIPS-approved cryptography: the add-on authenticates with an account holding only the trackme_broker role. Requires TrackMe 2.4.24 or later on the stack. Documentation: https://docs.trackme-solutions.com/product_guide/integ_broker.html

item.title: Whisper Security Infrastructure Graph Add-on - v2.0.1 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
# 2.0.1 release notes 2.0.1 fixes what several commands return and what the dashboard and Configuration page say. It adds no command and removes nothing. Install it over 2.0.0. Your account, API key and data-sharing acknowledgement carry over. Answers cached by 2.0.0 are not reused: each command asks Whisper again, and the first `whisperenrich` search clears 2.0.0's rows from `whisper_graph_enrichment`, the collection its automatic lookup reads. It runs on Splunk 10.2 and 10.4 with `python.required = 3.13` only, as 2.0.0 did. ## New * `whisperlookup evidence=true` adds `whisper_other_lists` (popularity lists, allowlists and other lists that are not threats) and `whisper_unclassified_lists` (listings Whisper has not classified). `whisper_sources` now holds threat feeds only. * `whisperenrich` domain rows carry `whisper_geo_country` and `whisper_geo_city`, for the address `whisper_asn` describes. ## Improved * The Investigate dashboard lists threat feeds apart from other lists, and names the allowlisting behind a benign verdict, such as a popularity rank. * Its tables no longer show rows no search fills, such as RPKI and MOAS. * `whisperflush mode=expired` and `whisperevict` also clear expired rows from `whisper_graph_enrichment`, with one result row per collection. * The Account tab's upgrade count also looks for `whisper:threat_intel`, `whisper:watchlist`, `whisper_domain_lookup` and `whisper_ip_lookup`, and runs again on your first save after the upgrade. * Each `whisperenrich` search logs its last request id for Whisper support. ## Fixed * On a `whisperenrich` domain row, `whisper_is_threat` is the domain's own verdict, as on `whisperlookup`. 2.0.0 read `true` if any of its addresses was flagged; that count is in `whisper_is_threat_address_count` with `detail=full`. * `whisper_registrar` and `whisper_prev_registrar` show the registrar's name, such as `MarkMonitor Inc.`, not an id such as `iana:292`. A domain that never changed registrar no longer gets the registrar-change risk factor. * `whisper_cname_target` is the last name in the CNAME chain, the same on every run. * If Whisper declines to score an indicator or sends no answer, `whisper_threat_score` reads `N/A` and `whisper_threat_level` is empty, where 2.0.0 could show `0.0` and `UNKNOWN`. An indicator with no data still reads `UNKNOWN`. * With `detail=full`, `whisper_threat_feed_ids` lists threat feeds only. * A `whisperenrich` row with no answer reads `whisper_status=degraded` with `context-incomplete` instead of `ok`. Rows answered under an API key Whisper did not accept read `degraded` with `key-not-accepted` in `whisperenrich` and `whisperschema` too. `whisperenrich` caches neither. * An empty `whisperschema` answer returns one row instead of none. * An empty `whisperquery` query says the query is empty instead of refusing it as a write. * An install upgraded from 1.0.0 with a user name and password in its hidden proxy URL can save the Settings tab again, and the save deletes that URL. The password was stored in clear text: change it on the proxy, then use the Proxy fields. * On Splunk Cloud, a refused Test connection asks for the time of the test and its message, not a request id the page does not show. * The packaged README and the `whisperenrich` help match what the add-on does, and the package drops an unused command-line helper from a bundled library.


Short Description:
Answer who runs an IP or domain, what shares its infrastructure and whether anyone has reported it, from the Splunk search bar. Five search commands, eight macros and one dashboard over Whisper Security's graph of internet infrastructure. No index, no scheduled search, no modular input. Needs a free API key.


Description:
An IP address or a domain lands in your search results and you have ten minutes to decide whether it matters. Who runs it. What else sits on the same infrastructure. Whether anyone has reported it before. This add-on answers those three questions from the Splunk search bar, against Whisper Security's graph of internet infrastructure: DNS, BGP, WHOIS, hosting, mail records and threat feeds, joined as one connected structure rather than a set of separate lookups. What you get: five search commands. whisperlookup puts a coverage-qualified verdict on events you already have. whisperenrich attaches the infrastructure behind an indicator to those same events: routing and network, hosting, and feed listings. whisperquery runs a parameterised Cypher query and returns the rows as events. whisperschema describes what is in the graph. whisperflush manages the local cache. Eight macros answer the next questions without any Cypher: the verdict for one indicator and the graph's own explanation of it, registered look-alike domains, whether a hostname's CNAME points at a service nobody holds any more, registration history, and the CNAME and SPF chains. The eighth makes no call: it turns the two fields below into a word for a results table. One dashboard, Investigate, opens a single hostname, IP address or URL in three bands: the verdict and what it rests on, the network that routes it, and the neighbouring hosts that share its address. Every row says how sure it is: two separate fields, and neither stands in for the other. Coverage says what the graph knows about the indicator, with one of six values: Evidence of malice; Contested evidence; Listing stopped; Not answered; No data; or Checked, not malicious. Call status says whether the request that asked completed, and carries the sentence for what to do next. An empty panel is an answer about the indicator, not a failure of the add-on. What it needs: a Whisper Security API key, free from https://console.whisper.security/sign-up?source=splunk-addon-listing. Outbound HTTPS to graph.whisper.security on port 443. Splunk 10.2 or later, on a search head. Setup is one page: enter the key, tick the box that authorises indicators to leave your deployment, save. The key is held in Splunk's encrypted storage/passwords and nowhere else. What it never does: it writes to no index and ships no indexes.conf. It ships no modular input and no scheduled search, so it makes no call out of your deployment unless someone runs a search. It claims no CIM mapping, because it indexes nothing to map. It ships no detection content. Until an administrator ticks the consent box, every command in the deployment sends nothing and says so on the row.

Build, import, validate, and package Splunk add-ons through a visual browser UI — no CLI. Create inputs (REST/shell/Python), alert actions, source types, field extractions, CIM mappings, lookups, and setup pages on the UCC Framework, run inputs and alerts in the browser to inspect their output, validate with AppInspect, and package for Splunkbase in one click.


Description:
TA Studio is a browser-based visual workbench for building Splunk® add-ons (TAs) on the Universal Configuration Console (UCC) Framework — without touching the command line. Authoring a quality add-on normally means working with the ucc-gen CLI, hand-editing globalConfig.json and a web of .conf files, and running AppInspect and packaging from a terminal. TA Studio replaces that workflow with a guided, point-and-click interface that runs entirely inside your own Splunk instance. From one UI you can create and manage data inputs (REST API, shell command, or Python modular inputs), alert actions (including Enterprise Security adaptive response), source types, field extractions with a live regex builder, CIM data model mappings, setup pages (accounts, proxy, logging), CSV lookups, and event types. You can import existing Splunk Add-on Builder and conf-based add-ons to modernize them, run inputs and alert actions right in the browser to inspect the events and output they produce, validate with AppInspect (including cloud checks) and review the results, then package a Splunkbase-ready archive in one click. TA Studio also includes built-in AI assistance to help you generate and refine input and alert-action code as you work. It otherwise runs entirely within your local Splunk environment: your add-on projects are not collected, transmitted, or stored outside your instance, and AI features send only the content you choose to submit to your selected AI provider.

Description:
Most inventories can tell you what is installed. Few can tell you what the maker has stopped patching. This app adds that answer to the software and operating-system inventory you already collect in Splunk. The eollookup search command takes a product and a version from each row and adds: - whether the version is still supported, close to its end, or past end of life - the end-of-life date, with days remaining or days past - the EOL Risk Score (0 to 100) and its letter grade - whether the product has an entry in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog - where the date comes from, as a link you can open Full patch versions work: 18.19.0 is answered for the Node.js 18 line, 8.6 for RHEL 8. When a build could belong to more than one support line (SQL Server service packs, Firefox standard and ESR) the app does not pick one. It says so and lists the candidates. Nothing is guessed. Included: - eollookup, a streaming search command that batches lookups, so a search over many hosts makes few API calls - an overview dashboard: past end of life, ending within 180 days, past end of life with a CISA KEV entry, and rows that could not be matched - four example reports, none scheduled - a setup page that stores your API key in Splunk's encrypted credential store Coverage is 700+ products: operating systems, databases, language runtimes, frameworks, network and security appliances. Every date names its source. What leaves your environment: product names and version strings, sent over HTTPS to api.endoflife.ai when the command runs. No host names, users, IP addresses or event data. The app works without an API key at the anonymous limits until November 16, 2026; from then the API needs a key for every lookup. item.title: Hurricane Labs Add-on for Windows PowerShell Transcript - v0.2.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\## 0.2.0 Tested on Splunk Enterprise 9.4.3, 10.4.1 and 10.6.1. Supports Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.x transcripts. \### Fixes \- Events are now timestamped with the session's Start time instead of the transcript file's last-modified time. \- PowerShell 7 transcripts ("PowerShell transcript start") now split into one event per session, and their end blocks are dropped. CRLF and LF files both work. \- Transcripts in other languages now parse: Windows PowerShell 5.1 on non-English Windows and PowerShell 7.6.6+ translate the header, so parsing now goes by the header's layout instead of English words. \- user, domain, username, runas_user and runas_domain keep dots, spaces and $ in names, and handle NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. \- std_out now starts after the header for both PowerShell versions. \- computer/dest no longer spans several lines when the machine name is blank. \### Eventtype changes (search time) \- powershell_encoded_command matches every -EncodedCommand abbreviation (-e, -ec, -enc ...) and the / forms (/e, /enc ...), but only when followed by a base64 UTF-16LE payload. -Encoding abbreviations and other tools' -e (docker, git, sed) no longer match. \- powershell_command needs -Command (or -c, -com ...) on a line that runs powershell or pwsh. -ComputerName, -ComObject, Invoke-Command, Get-Command, python -c and bash -c no longer match. \- powershell_nslookup_txt also matches -type\=txt and -querytype\=txt. \- powershell_registry also matches Get-ItemProperty -Path HK... and Set-Location HK... \### New \- CIM Endpoint.Processes field names: dest, process, process_id, process_path, process_name, action. \- powershell_transcript_session eventtype for opting in to the CIM Endpoint data model (no data model tags by default; see the README). \- Splunk Cloud readiness: \[id] stanza in app.conf and sc_admin write access. \### Upgrade notes \- Timestamp, line-breaking and end-block changes apply only to newly indexed data. \- Eventtype changes apply at search time, so they change what existing saved searches and alerts on these eventtypes match. \- Events are now dated by session start, which can be well before Splunk receives them. Scheduled searches with short lookbacks should search by arrival time, e.g. \_index_earliest\=-20m. \- Transcript times have no time zone. A single forwarder reading transcripts from several time zones needs a per-host TZ (see the README). \### Known limitations \- A session is one event, and Splunk drops everything past 256 KB (TRUNCATE), so commands after very long output aren't indexed. \- Command output that reproduces a transcript header (e.g. Get-Content of another transcript) splits the session there, and later commands take that header's fields and start time. \- Full list in the README.


Description:
This app provides knowledge objects for working with Windows PowerShell transcript logs. In addition to field extractions, a number of event types are included to support threat hunting use cases. You will need to configure your Windows systems to log PowerShell transcripts in order to benefit from this app. This logging is not enabled by default in Windows. These logs, once generated, should be collected via a file input and forwarded to Splunk. Additional information on the configuration of this app is available here: www.hurricanelabs.com/splunk-tutorials/splunk-tutorial-powershell-transcription-logging This app is also available on GitHub: https://github.com/HurricaneLabs/TA-powershell_transcript

## Version 1.2.7 ### Text Reliability Improvements * Improved monitoring persistence resilience when parsed records contain invalid or corrupted text. * Invalid parsed records are now isolated so unaffected monitoring records can continue updating. * Added field-specific validation for corrupted replacement characters, malformed UTF-8 text and unpaired surrogates. * Valid Turkish UTF-8 characters remain fully supported. * Improved Manage Targets error reporting for invalid text fields. * Added the same text-validation protections to Email Subject Settings. * All six notification subject templates are validated before configuration is written. * Existing corrupt target fields can be corrected without deleting or recreating the target. * No automatic text replacement, transliteration or legacy encoding fallback is performed. ### Compatibility * No KV Store schema changes. * No Search Head Cluster behavior changes. * No scheduler cadence changes. * No runtime lock or retry behavior changes. * Existing target IDs and KV records remain compatible. ### Known Limitation Undecodable command input streams that fail before row parsing still abort the invocation and require upstream encoding correction.

Description:

The app supports target-based continuity monitoring, interruption detection, recovery tracking, maintenance and redundancy-aware handling, and operational dashboards for monitoring status and history. Version 1.2.1 adds Mass Interruption monitoring with Host Count and Percentage thresholds, scoped policies for host_index, host_index_source and host_index_sourcetype targets, interruption/reminder/recovery email notifications, notification delivery visibility, KV Store-backed runtime state, and improved Search Head Cluster readiness.
